items.excerpt: ## Sen. Chris Van Hollen Will Challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate Majority Leader Nov 13, 2026 Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen said Thursday he will challenge New York’s Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader when Democrats retake control of both chambers of Congress in January. This follows historic gains for Democrats in last week’s midterm elections. They’ll now control at least 255 seats in the House of Representatives and 55 in the Senate. This is Senator Van Hollen speaking on MS NOW. > Sen. Chris Van Hollen: “And it wasn’t only a rejection of Donald Trump and his corruption and his wars and his cruelty. It was also about a call for a larger change to take on a broken economic system that’s rigged in favor of the very wealthy against working people and that’s fueled by a corrupt political system. And the call was really to reject the status quo and to reject business as usual. And to do that, I think we need new leadership.” Van Hollen is the first Democratic senator to launch a leadership challenge since 1994. His bid was quickly endorsed by Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed and Vermont independent Senator Bernie Sanders. ... ## Nvidia’s Colette Kress to Serve as Interim CEO as Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Scandals Nvidia CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang has resigned. The chip maker says its longtime chief financial officer, Colette Kress, will serve as interim CEO while Nvidia’s board of directors searches for a permanent replacement. Huang stepped down as Reuters reported he’d had an intimate relationship with a second employee, whom Reuters did not name. That follows reports that Huang had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who U.S. intelligence officials claim was spying for Beijing as part of a Chinese intelligence operation seeking to acquire advanced computer chips, which are banned by U.S. export controls. Huang reportedly helped the alleged spy acquire at least $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips for China via a Singapore-based cloud computing company called Megaspeed International. Meanwhile, Bloomberg reports Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before House lawmakers in a closed-door hearing later this month. Nvidia has lost nearly $2 trillion in market capitalization since its all-time high in early October. We’ll have more on this story after headlines. ## Microsoft Outage Disrupts Communications for Millions Across 74 Countries In more technology news, Microsoft is scrambling to fix a major outage that’s disrupted communication for millions of people across at least 74 countries since Thursday morning. The outage has cut off access to Microsoft’s Outlook, Teams and the AI assistant Copilot. ## Iran Says It Blew Up U.S. Early-Warning Radar as Trump Declares, “We Don’t Need a Deal with Iran” Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says it destroyed a U.S. early-warning radar system in Bahrain in retaliation for a U.S. strike on a telecommunications tower in southern Iran. Officials also claimed four attacks on oil tankers in ​the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, following strikes on a pair of supertankers one day earlier. Iran’s attacks came as President Trump on Thursday sidelined Vice President JD Vance as the top U.S. negotiator with Iran. Trump said in a social media post he’d directed Vance to instead focus on fighting what Trump called “corruption and crime” in Democratic-controlled cities and states. Trump wrote, “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” ... ## Russia and Ukraine Continue Deadly Strikes as U.S. Envoys Meet Putin and Zelensky Russia and Ukraine traded drone and missile attacks overnight, despite a diplomatic push by the Trump administration that’s purportedly seeking an end to the conflict. The violence came after President Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow, followed by a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Dublin. Both Russia and Ukraine agreed to a prisoner swap that Zelensky called the largest since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Meanwhile, Zelensky has accused Elon Musk’s SpaceX of once again restricting service to Starshield, the military-grade version of the Starlink internet satellite constellation, which Ukraine uses for drone attacks. ## Infant Dies of Hypothermia in Gaza as Calls Grow for Israel to Allow Imports of Winter Supplies In Gaza, a Palestinian infant has died from hypothermia after Israeli attacks left his family displaced and living in a tent in Khan Younis. Kinan Ahmed Raqiq was just 9 months old. His death came as Israel continued to impose severe restrictions on imports of fuel and winter supplies into Gaza. U.N. humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher says 150,000 tents remain stuck in warehouses at Gaza’s borders, even as some 350,000 displaced Palestinians face heavy rain, flooding and plummeting temperatures. On Thursday, a group of 49 nations issued a joint call for Israel to ease restrictions on shelter, fuel, water, sanitation and medical supplies to Gaza. The United States did not sign the statement. This is Britain’s ambassador to the U.N., Sarah MacIntosh, speaking from U.N. headquarters. ... Here in New York, tenant advocates are demanding justice after what they described as the preventable collapse of an apartment building in Brooklyn that killed at least eight people, including two children, and injured at least 23 others Wednesday.

items.title: Bessent, Fed’s Goolsbee divided on role of energy shock in inflation By Reuters
items.excerpt: Published Nov 13, 2026, 09:02 AM Updated Nov 13, 2026, 10:42 AM ... WASHINGTON, Nov 13 (Reuters) - US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Friday that the Federal Reserve should not hike rates because of inflation driven by an "energy supply shock" tied to the Iran war, comments made to CNBC and promptly contradicted on the network by Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, who said price pressures were building far beyond what could be explained by high oil prices. "I think the Fed should understand that this is an energy supply shock," while the underlying US economy is very strong, Bessent said in an interview on CNBC. "So I think that to hike too much into an energy supply shock when it’s coming down, these are very noisy numbers...You know, the Fed’s supposed to look into the future, not look in the rearview mirror." Shortly afterwards, the network hosted Goolsbee, a regular guest on CNBC’s morning Squawk Box show, who said that inflation was not just due to energy, but had spread to the service sector and areas like medical care that are not usually responsive to the price of oil, and was also elevated through strong demand tied to the AI data center buildout. "I respect the secretary and I am trying to figure out the same thing he is trying to figure out, which is how persistent is this inflation? The tariff inflation and oil price shock were supposed to have gone away by now and it hasn’t," Goolsbee said. "One puzzle is why have those supply shocks been as persistent as they have been. A second thing is if demand is overheating and that is contributing to inflation, that is more worrisome... Services inflation, which is probably not coming from tariffs or oil, is one of the more troubling aspects of the inflation reports we have been getting." While not committing to a rate hike, he said the Fed "has definitely got work to do to continue to reestablish its credibility." ... Fed policymakers were open to the possibility they could "look through" supply-driven inflation at the start of the US war with Iran. But as inflation remained lodged above the Fed’s target, concern about it grew, as did support for rate hikes. Research meanwhile opened a different window on the relationship between oil prices and US inflation. Because the US is an energy exporter, higher global oil prices can filter through to the economy in the form of higher corporate profits and wages, providing a source of inflation beyond supply issues that can’t be easily ignored by the central bank. Recent stronger-than-expected jobs and inflation reports have further bolstered the case for more Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, and even prompted some officials to discuss the need for a larger-than-typical half-percentage-point increase at the central bank’s coming December 8-9 meeting. "We have had signs of trouble now for several months in a row if you look at how broad-based the inflation is," Goolsbee said. "In categories that are not driven by oil prices and not driven by tariffs, you are still seeing stalled progress and in some cases going the wrong way ... That is not going away no matter what happens to the price of oil." "Are we on a path back to 2%? My feeling right now is we are not and we’ve got to deal with that," Goolsbee said. "Conventional wisdom says do everything you can to prevent demand overheating," Goolsbee said, with coming data on inflation the key to whether the Fed needs a faster pace of rate increases.

items.title: PPI inflation report October 2026:
items.excerpt: Published Fri, Nov 13 2026 8:31 AM EST Updated An Hour Ago ... Key Points - The producer price index, a measure of wholesale prices, rose 0.3% in October, slightly less than the 0.4% forecast. - On an annual basis, PPI surged 6.5%, the biggest increase since November 2022. ... Wholesale prices increased less than expected in October, but inflation pressures persisted and the Federal Reserve is likely still on target for an interest rate increase soon. The producer price index, which measures the prices domestic producers get for their products before they reach the consumer, rose a seasonally adjusted 0.3% for the month, against the Dow Jones consensus for a 0.4% increase, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Friday. Stripping out food and energy, core PPI posted a 0.3% gain, meeting expectations. On an annual basis, headline PPI accelerated 6.5%, up 0.2 percentage point for the highest annual rate since November 2022. The report comes just a few weeks ahead of the Federal Reserve's next policy meeting, Dec. 8-9. Markets are fully pricing in a quarter percentage point increase in the central bank's key overnight borrowing rate, with slight odds that the Federal Open Market Committee might opt for a half-point hike. Stock market futures added to gains following the release while Treasury yields were mixed. Earlier this week, the BLS reported that inflation at the cash register was hotter than expected. The headline consumer price index saw a 0.4% increase in October while core was up 0.3%, both 0.1 percentage point higher than expected. Because of the government shutdown in October 2025, the BLS couldn't collect some data and refrained from putting out a 12-month inflation figure for CPI. However, the figures showed that the Fed remains a good distance from its 2% inflation goal. "Today's PPI data – which shows some signs of improving, albeit still too-high – is unlikely to change the Fed's approach in December because the CPI data was already outside their comfort zone," said Chris Zaccarelli, chief investment officer for Northlight Asset Management. Moreover, policymakers are beginning to worry that inflation generated by the Iran war and higher fuel prices, along with President Donald Trump's tariffs, are beginning to spread through the economy. The Fed generally would look through such price pressures as temporary, but the breadth of inflation could indicate that inflation is becoming more entrenched. "We've had some signs of trouble now for several months in a row," Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said in a CNBC interview Friday. "If you look at how broad-based the inflation is, it's not just that we're above the target and have been for some time. It's that in categories that are not driven by oil prices and not driven by tariffs, you're still seeing stalled progress and in some cases going the wrong way." Stripping out food, energy and trade services, PPI saw an increase of 0.5% in October. Goods prices increased 0.5% in October, with more than 60% of that move driven by goods excluding food and energy, which actually saw a 0.1% decrease. On an annual basis, the goods index jumped 10.2%, the biggest 12-month surge since October 2022. Final demand services prices increased 0.2%, most of which was linked to transportation and warehousing services, and within that category a 3.9% gain in truck transportation of freight. "We've been above 2% for almost six years, and while it sometimes we were making progress, lately we're not making any progress, and if anything, it's going the wrong way," Goolsbee said. "Inflation is rising; it's proved far more persistent than we predicted at the beginning from the supply shocks." Other items in the PPI report also showed multiyear gains. Prices for intermediate processed goods soared 14.6% from October 2025, the biggest annual gain since July 2022. Intermediate prices for services posted a 6.9% increase, the most since November 2022.

items.title: New Music Friday November 13: U2, Dolly Parton, Enrique Iglesias, Offset, Wiz Khalifa, Fall Out Boy and More | Entertainment Tonight
items.excerpt: Published: 8:17 AM PST, November 13, 2026 ## Check out some of ET's favorite new music of the week! Happy New Music Friday! The weekend is here, which means more streaming, new playlists and the best that music has to offer -- and ET has you covered for everything in between. U2 and Dolly Parton's new song and Dolly's final recording "Torn" is out now from U2's 16th studio album, Carnaval De Luz. The song was co-written by U2, Dolly and Johnny McDaid and is a tender country song detailing broken family ties that holds wider resonances. Dolly recorded the song in Nashville in June this year, making it her final recorded vocal performance prior to her passing in August. Ahead of the track's release, a country version titled 'Torn' (Kent Wells Version) premiered on country radio on November 12. The Country Music Association and ABC have announced more performers for The 60th Annual CMA Awards. Taylor Swift will be performing, marking her much-anticipated return 13 years since her last performance. Luke Combs, Vince Gill, Megan Moroney, Mumford & Sons, Chris Stapleton, Lainey Wilson and Stephen Wilson Jr. have also been added to the lineup. Brothers Osborne, Luke Bryan, Halestorm, HARDY and Marcus King will come together to celebrate Brooks & Dunn, this year's recipients of the CMA Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award. Country Music's Biggest Night will air live on November 18 on ABC and Disney+ and next day on Hulu. P!NK has announced her first ever Las Vegas residency at Sphere, becoming the first solo female artist to headline Sphere. Promoted by Live Nation, she will bring perform at Sphere beginning September 29. ... Rosalía made history at Latin GRAMMY Awards again as she won Album of the Year for her album, Lux, marking the third time she has taken home the honor and making her the first woman to win the award as a lead artist that many times. Janet Jackson made a surprise appearance presenting Daddy Yankee with the Person of the Year award. Daddy Yankee was also honored at the 2026 Latin Recording Academy Person of the Year Gala and recognized for his nearly three-decade career as a driving force behind the globalization of reggaeton and for his humanitarian efforts. ... Olivia Dean was announced as Apple Music's Artist of the Year, recognizing her undeniable leap to stardom. She is the first UK artist to receive this honor. Olivia shared, "I love making music. It's the best thing in the world. I think being Apple's Artist of the Year feels really amazing. To be recognized as an artist that's made an impact is really cool." Alex Warren has announced his Finding (More) Family On The Road 2027 World Tour with special guests Bebe Stockwell and Faouzia. Alex made the announcement in a video with Eric Stonestreet declaring he is adding 26 more shows. Promoted by Live Nation, the 26-city North American leg kicks off on April 5 at Paycom Center in Oklahoma City, making stops in New York, Tampa, Raleigh and more before wrapping up in Birmingham, AL on May 16. ... Fall Out Boy released a new song "ACES" which marks their first new original single in over three years. They also announced a new global headline tour, Twilight of the Punks, which will be the biggest tour of their career with 36 dates performing at stadiums and arenas across Europe, the UK and North America in 2027. Promoted by Live Nation, the tour kicks off May 17 at Prague's O2 Arena. To celebrate their tour announcement, Fall Out Boy gave a surprise pop up show at Koreatown in Los Angeles this week. Thousands of fans showed up for the eight-song set including the live debut of their new single "ACES."
